a project that belongs to a solution every epic is a solution epic, created in every member at once and open to tasks from any member, and a second task may hold a shared tracker issue when it sits in the same solution epic in a different member project.\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022h9k epic add in a project that belongs to a solution creates a solution epic with no home project: its events are written to every member project\\u0027s ledger this node holds, receiving nodes de-duplicate by event id, and a project linked into the solution later receives the solution\\u0027s existing epics through the catch-up mechanism.\u0022,\u0022A project inside a solution cannot hold a project-only epic; a project outside any solution behaves exactly as today, and existing epics are untouched.\u0022,\u0022A task from any member project may join a solution epic at add or revise: the same-project membership check (EpicIdResolver.ResolveForMembershipAsync) becomes same-solution for a solution epic.\u0022,\u0022epic show and epic list compose member tasks across projects grouped by project, and a node shows only the tasks of projects it has joined, because tasks still replicate through their own project\\u0027s ledger alone.\u0022,\u0022The one-live-task-per-issue refusal (TaskAddCommand.RefuseSecondAdoptionAsync, reached from --from-issue, --from-jira, task link-issue and task link-jira) admits a second task when that task is in the same solution epic as the holder and in a different member project; every other case still refuses with the same message, and closeout\\u0027s existing all-linked-tasks-done rule (CloseoutEngine.AllOtherLinkedTasksClosedOutAsync) is what closes the issue.\u0022,\u0022Closing a solution epic stays an explicit human act with a reason; nothing closes one automatically.\u0022,\u0022Unit tests cover the fan-out decision, de-duplication on receipt, the same-solution membership check and the shared-issue admission; no test creates a branch or touches GitHub.\u0022,\u0022docs/concepts.md, docs/scope.md and the hall9k-cli-reference skill describe solution epics and the shared-issue rule.\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Multi-repo projects: one hall9k project whose work spans several GitHub repositories (for example a backend API and infrastructure repo, a frontend repo, and a couple of others). Today a project has exactly one repo; a new project of Brian\\u0027s needs several.\\n\\nDiscovery for idea f8212260: findings.md and journal.md in the idea\\u0027s workspace. Brian\\u0027s rulings (2026-10-29): no home project; an epic in a solution project is always solution-wide so every member knows of it before any task exists; a second task may hold one tracker issue only inside the same solution epic and a different member project (the case of one issue needing a backend and a frontend change, raised by the Linear connector discovery, idea 5d12221a). This is new replication plumbing: a solution-scoped event that fans out to several ledgers; size it as medium, not small. Stacked on the solution base task because it reads the SolutionMembership type and the Solution record that task introduces.\\n\\nDiscovery workspace (research notes, gathered files, and prototypes solution membership reaches the joining node through the first member it joins, so h9k solution show on that node lists every member afterwards, joined or not.\u0022,\u0022Unit tests cover the generated command sequence and the per-member reporting; no test creates a branch, mints a real invite against GitHub, or touches a remote.\u0022,\u0022docs/operations.md (or its successor) and the
